The counting bound 2.1 then becomes unconditional, and 2.2 includes the full difference set among the finitely many nonempty S. The final diagonal construction 4.1 therefore also achieves the total-rate face.

In 1.1 the conditional entropy expands as a difference of continuous finite entropies using 0 ln0=0. In 2.1 unsupported marginal letters never occur in a typical candidate; all logarithms are restricted to PUi>0. Thus zero masses introduce neither undefined logs nor an omitted contribution to the packing bound.

For k=1 the complementary-selector restriction is vacuous by the Statement, and 3.1 explicitly uses only the independent side-information block when J=[k]. A singleton S represents absent side information; its entropy is zero and the fan/exponent calculations 1.1–2.1 reduce accordingly.

A deterministic marginal codeword or a constant side variable is admitted by the finite target law. In 2.1 its only supported symbol has log probability zero. The rate condition still supplies eta>0; even when its information exponent is zero, sufficiently many bins make the collision factor in 3.1 decay.

Proof 1.1 chooses one real tolerance from continuity for each of finitely many nonempty J. Proof 3.1 sums a finite set of candidate index combinations with independent uniform bin labels, and 4.1 sums finitely many subsets. It does not select witnesses from an arbitrary nonempty family.

The revised assertion is a sufficient packing bound under strict rate slack and sufficiently small fixed tolerance. Proof 3.1 bounds the expected wrong-tuple count and 4.1 bounds its probability; neither step claims the slack is necessary for the error to vanish.

The vanishing-error consequence is one-way: Markov bounds existence of a wrong tuple by its expected count in 4.1. The Statement makes no converse from absence of false tuples to the displayed rate inequalities or selector independence.

The new 1.1 proves nonnegativity directly from ln s<=s-1, including omitted zero masses. In 2.1 the bound -t ln t<=2 sqrt(t) explicitly extends entropy to zero coordinates. If X has one value, U may be constant and a reconstruction minimizing distortion is a map of Y alone, so Dmin=Dmax and 3.1 makes the feasible function identically zero. Constant Y is also admitted: the finite channel simplexes and decoder maps in 2.1 still form the same compact parameter space.

The added finite-entropy continuity calculation in 2.1 includes deterministic laws and zero channel entries. When Dmin=Dmax, 3.1 explicitly uses the zero-rate minimizing decoder and proves the entire feasible function is zero rather than dividing by Dmax-Dmin.

At Dmin, 2.1 uses nested closed compact channel sets to rule out a downward jump. At Dmax, 3.1 bounds the value by the linear interpolation from Dmin and hence proves the limit is zero. The same final step now also identifies D<Dmin as an empty feasible set with value +infinity.

The minimizers invoked in 1.2 are supplied by the finite auxiliary-cardinality compactness theorem, and only two are chosen. The decoder-map union in 2.1 is finite; its nested-intersection argument uses compactness, not a simultaneous selection from the nonempty Kj.

The final 3.1 distinguishes infeasible, interior, zero-rate and coincident-endpoint domains; those conclusions do not assert a converse characterizing a test channel from continuity or convexity. No reverse implication is part of the Statement.

Its Remarks supply U=X with a pointwise minimizing reconstruction at Dmin; thus 2.1 has feasible compact channel sets at every D>=Dmin. The genuinely empty feasible region D<Dmin is now explicitly treated in 3.1 as value +infinity.

The fixed pair in 1.1 must lie in a supported typical set. Its underlying probability alphabets cannot be empty, and its blocklength is sufficiently large. The event of no matching word may occur but is a failed search event, not an empty input-law case; 3.1 bounds precisely that event.

eta is strictly positive, the chosen tolerances satisfy 0<delta_in<delta_out, and R has strict slack. Under Qn in the revised 1.1, zero-mass input pairs are absent and zero conditional output probabilities cannot be sampled. On every positive target triple, P(u|v)>0 as well as P(u|x,v)>0, so the Qn/Cn ratio in 2.1 is defined; zero atoms never create a division or log of zero.

With V constant the conditional information becomes I(X;U), and the fixed v word is unique. If U is a singleton, both Qn and Cn in 1.1 put mass one on its only word, the exponent is zero, and any R>eta makes the independent-trial success assertion true. The proof includes these finite laws.

The revised 2.1 chooses a tolerance by continuity of one finite linear likelihood functional; it does not construct or select a codebook witness there. Step 3.1 computes the probability of at least one match among finitely many conditionally independent codewords. No choice principle is invoked.
